item.title: Dogashima Sea Caves: West Izu's Skylight Grotto and Boat Tours — Guide
item.description: Dogashima, on the Izu Peninsula’s wild west coast, is famous for its white volcanic tuff cliffs and wave-carved sea caves, the striking result of layered volcanic ash sculpted by the sea. The highlight is Tensodo, a skylight cave whose roof has collapsed to leave a natural round opening, sending a shaft of light onto the blue-green water below; small sightseeing boats cruise into the cave itself, while a clifftop path above lets you peer down through the skylight, and at low tide a tombolo land bridge appears to a nearby island.

item.title: Nagatoro Gorge: Traditional Boat Rides Through Dramatic Rock Cliffs — Guide
item.description: Nagatoro Gorge, where the Arakawa River cuts through a series of distinctive layered rock formations known as Iwadatami (‘rock tatami mats’), is one of Saitama’s most scenic and photographed landscapes, designated a National Natural Monument for its striking crystalline schist cliffs. Traditional wooden boats, operated by local boatmen, carry visitors along a roughly 6 km stretch of the gorge, passing beneath towering rock walls and through gentle rapids, a tradition dating back over a century.

item.title: Hotokegaura: Aomori's Surreal Buddha Cliffs — Guide
item.description: Hotokegaura, the ‘Buddha Shore’, is one of Japan’s most extraordinary coastlines — white dolomite columns rising up to 100 m from the Sea of Japan along the Shimokita Peninsula, their shapes likened to Buddhist saints. Reachable only by seasonal boat, it stays almost unknown to foreign visitors. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Sai Village, Shimokita, Aomori Hours Boat tours ~Apr–Oct, daytime Admission Boat tour ~¥2,000+ Time needed 1.

item.title: Lake Towada: Aomori's Crater Lake & Boat Tours — Guide
item.description: Lake Towada is a double volcanic crater lake of astonishing clarity, sitting 320 m above sea level on the Aomori–Akita border. The lakeside ‘Maidens’ statue, a 50-minute sightseeing cruise, and some of Japan’s finest mid-October foliage make it the natural climax of a Towada–Oirase trip. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Towada, Aomori (Akita border) Hours Lake open; cruises ~9:00–16:00 Admission Free; cruise ~¥1,500 Time needed 1.

item.title: Choshi Whale & Dolphin Watching Guide: Tours & Access
item.description: Few people realise you can go whale and dolphin watching within easy reach of Tokyo — but the rich waters off Choshi, where the warm Kuroshio current meets the cold Oyashio off the Boso Peninsula’s northeastern tip, are one of Japan’s most reliable spots. Boat tours head out from Choshi port to look for large pods of dolphins (often hundreds at a time) and, in season, whales such as minke, Bryde’s and even sperm whales.
